title: Bomb, Blast, and Crush Injuries

source.boundary: Actual Bomb, Blast, and Crush Injuries title lower left PDF12/printed30 through references left column PDF17/printed35 above actual Chemical Disasters title. Adjacent chapters on shared pages excluded.
source.verification: Selected vocabulary and actual chapter boundaries, not clinical recommendations, treatment guidance or current practice validation.

scope: Twenty selected terms. Offline visual vocabulary candidates, not exhaustive chapter coverage, medical anchors, narration or image-generation prompts. Newly recorded does not imply original invention.

source_wording_notes.shearing: Term appears in Chapter7 blast mechanisms on printed30.
source_wording_notes.air embolism: Air-specific source term reuses Chapter3 gas embolism family cue; does not imply every gas is air.
source_wording_notes.open globe injuries: Exact phrase occurs in ocular injuries prose on printed32.

entries.cue: Large sheep-shearing shears sliding across and cutting layered fabric.
entries.reason: Shears provide a familiar word/action cue. Not a literal blast mechanism model or tissue physics lesson.

entries.cue: Metal can visibly collapsing inward with inward-pointing arrows.
entries.cue_scope: Inward collapse rather than outward explosion
entries.reason: Direction is visible rather than encoded by damage alone. Not a quantitative or complete tissue-mechanism explanation.

entries.cue: Damaged lung model inside a transparent pressure chamber with a conspicuously high gauge.
entries.reason: Pressure plus lung damage makes a learned category cue. Not a pressure threshold, exposure recommendation or a complete account of barotrauma.

entries.cue: Ear-shaped frame holding a drum with a conspicuous hole through its drum skin.
entries.reason: Familiar eardrum/drum double meaning and visible hole. Not diagnostic otoscopy, injury severity or evidence about other organs.

entries.cue: Air bubbles visibly trapped beneath a transparent skin-like cover on a mannequin arm.
entries.reason: Under/skin relationship carries the category. Not an etiology, physical examination finding or equivalence to pulmonary emphysema.

entries.cue: Butter lump lodged inside a vessel running through a lung-shaped model.
entries.cue_scope: Fat exemplar plus pulmonary vessel obstruction
entries.reason: Butter is a familiar fat token; the vessel location must be visible. Not dietary causation, literal butter in blood or a complete syndrome definition.

entries.cue: Wallpaper-like retinal lining peeling away from the back inner wall of a cutaway eyeball model.
entries.reason: Familiar peeling action supports a learned location cue. Not retinal anatomy precision, a diagnostic image or a repair technique.

entries.cue: Camera-lens token visibly displaced from its normal seat but still inside an intact transparent eyeball model.
entries.prior: New composition using existing camera-lens primitive in docs/sound-bridge-workshop-2.json.
entries.reason: Reuses familiar lens identity while adding displacement. Kept inside intact eye to avoid resembling extrusion/open globe. Newly recorded composition, not a newly invented primitive or precise anatomical rendering.

entries.cue: Eyeball-shaped world globe with prominent iris/pupil and a visibly split outer casing; geographic markings remain secondary.
entries.cue_scope: Globe plus open injury name cue
entries.prior: New composition using globe primitive in docs/sound-bridge-workshop.json.
entries.reason: Familiar world globe supplies the double meaning. Not every eye injury, a diagnostic drawing or an instruction to manipulate the eye.

entries.cue: Overpacked closed compartment bulging around its contents beneath a high pressure gauge.
entries.reason: Simple confined-pressure metaphor, not a diagnostic pressure value or a claim that all compartment syndromes are crush injuries.

entries.cue: Mannequin skin-like outer covering peeling off a study hand in the shape of a glove.
entries.reason: Clear removal action recovers the word without forcing sound fragments; skin-like covering avoids ordinary glove removal. Not restricted to hand injuries or a procedure demonstration.

entries.cue: Tiny pins and needles floating around a study-mannequin hand with tingling marks, without puncturing it.
entries.reason: Familiar sensory idiom, not literal puncture injury, every paresthesia quality or a disease-specific diagnosis.

entries.cue: Recognizable oxygen cylinder beside a transparent pressure chamber with its gauge pointing high.
entries.reason: Treatment-name identity only; cylinder is a mnemonic token, not a chamber setup or safety specification. No pressure, duration, indication or efficacy claim.

entries.cue: Nearly empty transparent reservoir connected in a closed circulation loop, with red liquid low at its bottom.
entries.reason: Low volume is visible. Not a laboratory threshold, proof of bleeding, dehydration equivalence or a fluid recommendation.

entries.cue: Large gas bubble lodged in a transparent branching vessel model.
entries.reason: Reuses gas embolism family cue for air-specific source term; not all gas emboli are air and no origin or circulation qualifier is encoded.

entries.cue: Air balloon outside a lung but inside a transparent chest shell.
entries.reason: Reuses prior pneumothoraces family cue; no tension physiology, diagnostic criteria or treatment.

entries.cue: Red liquid around a lung inside a transparent chest shell.
entries.reason: Consistent existing cue; no volume, severity or intervention encoded.
Established user-inspired candidate, not a dietary causal claim or serum threshold.

entries.cue: Kidney-shaped factory with conspicuously broken gears.
entries.reason: Existing category cue, not a mechanism or clinical diagnostic definition.
No economical bridge proposed. Train/axe/acid assembly needs excess sound repair and object count; no forced quota. Hold does not prove no useful association exists.
